Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.

meanings.note: About people. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind; good').
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!

заболеть.gloss: to fall ill, to get sick

meanings.en: to fall ill, to come down with an illness
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'болеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall ill, to get sick', paired with 'болеть'.

examples.text: Вчера он заболел и остался дома.
examples.trans: Yesterday he fell ill and stayed at home.

examples.text: А у меня учительница по математике заболела.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'order', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.

meanings.note: + с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'знакомиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to meet, to get acquainted', paired with 'знакомиться'.

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Ходила вокруг меня, как акула.

Кого о чём. Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упредить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to warn, notify in advance', paired with 'предупреждать'.

meanings.note: приветствую вас = greetings (formal)

meanings.en: to become hungry, work up an appetite
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'голодаться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to get hungry', forming an aspectual pair with 'голодать'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: After the walk we were hungry.
Our guests have gotten very hungry.

meanings.note: Проследить за + instrumental. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'следить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see to it, to keep an eye on', paired with 'следить'.

examples.trans: We'll keep an eye on it.
I'll keep an eye on the children.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
